title: Installation of ROCM compatible Torch
description:
## Feature

When using an AMD GPU I am unable to make use of GPU acceleration. According to the Python tabpfn package documentation, the correct way to get AMD (via ROCM) working is as per [these instructions](https://github.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn#installation):

"On Linux: Nvidia GPU support is automatically included. For AMD GPUs, first [install PyTorch with ROCm](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/), then install TabPFN. For example,

```python
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.2
pip install tabpfn
```
"

Searching through the R package source code I think the issue arises from letting Python tabpfn install the standard version of torch. I wonder if it's possible to split out the torch installation into a default and a rocm option, with the rocm option leading to something like:

```R
py_install(
  packages = c("torch", "torchvision", "torchaudio"),
  pip = TRUE,
  pip_options = c("--index-url", "https://pytorch.org")
)
```

Which, I think, should work as long as this is done before the Python tabpfn package is installed.

Thanks.

title: AttributeError: property 'stream' of '_StderrHandler' object has no setter on Windows with Python 3.12
description:
Hi thank you for creating the R version of tabpfn. I am having issues making the package to work. The setup:

Installed r-tabpfn virtualenv via install_tabpfn(python_version = "3.12")
Set RETICULATE_PYTHON in .Renviron to point to the virtualenv (necessary to override system Python 3.14 which reticulate otherwise discovers first)
Restarted R and ran:

```
tabpfn::tabpfn_initialize()
library(tabpfn)
predictors <- mtcars[, -1]
outcome    <- mtcars[, 1]
mod        <- tab_pfn(predictors, outcome)
```

Error

```
Error in py_call_impl(callable, call_args$unnamed, call_args$named) : 
  AttributeError: property 'stream' of '_StderrHandler' object has no setter
```

The error occurs regardless of whether version = "v2" or version = "v2.5" or v3 is passed to tab_pfn()
is_tab_pfn_installed() returns TRUE
tabpfn_download_models() completes successfully
The issue does not appear to be OpenMP-related as .Rprofile is empty

title: allow for users to choose the model checkpoint
description:
Hi all - 

TabPFN 2.5 was released November 2025. I was doing a bit of digging to figure out which model is used within tabpfn. I think a TabPFN model checkpoint is downloaded & cached when initiating a model fit. But it might be nice to let the user select which version of TabPFN to use when fitting/predicting. I think the python package grabs the most recent model by design (?) but users may want to keep this set to 2.0 for testing or if the license changes between model releases.

title: OpenMP causes R process to die
description:
We are working around an issue where pytorch and R both want to use OpenMP but have different library paths. 

If you load a package that uses OpenMP (directly or indirectly), the session will crash when you first pass data to or from python. 

The current solution is to load TabPFN, invoke python once (maybe use `reticulate::import("tabpfn")`) and then load other packages.
